2608.14391.title: Can We Defend Against AI-Generated Video Attacks on Real-World Crisis Events? A Systematic Evaluation of Detectors, Generators and Social Dissemination
2608.14391.paper_summary: Recent video generators can fabricate realistic depictions of wars, disasters, public emergencies, and other real-world crises, creating substantial risks of misinformation. Existing benchmarks, however, provide limited evidence on detector and generator behavior in such settings, including how detectability varies with generation conditions, how people perceive generated videos, and whether detectors remain reliable during social dissemination. To address this gap, we introduce RA-Bench, a benchmark for AI-generated video detection that uses Real videos as Anchors. RA-Bench contains 17,886 videos, comprising 1,830 real-video anchors across 10 social-risk categories and 16,056 generated clips from four open-source and five closed-source generators. Based on RA-Bench, we organize our evaluation along three dimensions. We first assess detector generalization across seven traditional detectors, ten zero-shot multimodal models under three review settings, and two MLLMs specifically fine-tuned on AI-generated video detection. Across these methods, none of the three detector families generalizes consistently across RA-Bench instances. We then examine how detectability varies with generation quality, conditioning information, and sampling seeds. These analyses show that generation properties affect detector families differently, while source-level detection patterns remain stable across seeds. Finally, we study human authenticity judgments and detector reliability during social dissemination. We find that videos that mislead people are also difficult for current detectors, and that social dissemination makes detection harder. Together, these findings show that current methods struggle to detect realistic AI-generated videos, highlighting the need for detectors robust to evolving video generators.
2608.14391.paper_summary_zh: 最近的視頻生成器能夠製作出真實的戰爭、災難、公共緊急事件及其他現實世界危機的逼真描繪，這造成了相當大的錯誤信息風險。 然而，現有的基準在這些情境下對檢測器和生成器行為提供的證據有限，包括可檢測性如何隨生成條件變化、人們如何感知生成的視頻，以及在社會傳播過程中檢測器是否保持可靠性。 為了解決這一空白，我們引入了RA-Bench，一個用真實視頻作為錨點的AI生成視頻檢測基準。 RA-Bench包含17,886個視頻，其中包括10個社會風險類別的1,830個真實視頻錨點和來自四個開源及五個閉源生成器的16,056個生成片段。 基於RA-Bench，我們沿著三個維度組織我們的評估。 我們首先評估七個傳統檢測器的檢測器泛化能力、在三個審查設定下的十個零樣本多模態模型，以及專門針對AI生成視頻檢測進行微調的兩個MLLM。 在這些方法中，三個檢測器家族在RA-Bench實例中的泛化能力並不一致。 然後，我們檢查可檢測性如何隨生成質量、條件信息和採樣種子變化。 這些分析顯示，生成屬性對檢測器家族的影響不同，而源級檢測模式在不同種子之間保持穩定。 最後，我們研究人類的真實性判斷和社會傳播過程中的檢測器可靠性。 我們發現，誤導人們的視頻對當前檢測器來說也很難檢測，並且社會傳播使檢測變得更加困難。 總體而言，這些發現顯示當前的方法在檢測真實的AI生成視頻方面面臨挑戰，突顯了對於能夠應對不斷演變的視頻生成器的檢測器的需求。
